main.1: Cohort construction and fixed-threshold evaluation. (A) BUS-BRA patients are split into development and internal testing; the development cohort selects each review cutoff at a 20 % target. (B) BrEaST contributes 252 patients after exclusion of four normal cases without a primary lesion mask. Each analysis patient contributes one image. Development cutoffs are transferred unchanged to the 1,103 internal and external test patients. Low-quality masks have initial-prediction Dice below 0.70 against the released reference. Counts refer to patients and their single initial masks.
main.2: Reference-informed prompting, observed SAM outputs and separate review scores. (A) The released image and reference from BrEaST case001 [10] define the initial box after 10 % expansion per side. Actual archived initial, left-, right-, up- and down-prompt masks are shown in their full image field; white is foreground. Shifts are 5 % of the clipped initial width or height. (B) Frozen SAM ViT-B encodes each image once and uses the shared embedding for five single-mask predictions. (C) Method A is one minus initial-mask predicted IoU; method B is one minus the mean initial-to-shifted mask Dice. Each score is evaluated separately against its locked development cutoff. The reference-derived prompt represents known-location evaluation.
main.3: Prespecified patient-level contrasts. Points show differences in percentage points; horizontal bars show original two-sided 95 % Newcombe method 10 confidence intervals. H1 compares Method A low-quality detection in the BrEaST external test cohort with the BUS-BRA internal holdout. H2 compares Method A simulated review fractions between those cohorts. H3 compares low-quality detection for Method B minus Method A among the same 16 external low-quality patients and uses the original paired interval. H2 and H3 intervals are nominal without multiplicity adjustment. Low quality is Dice <0.70. Numerators and denominators are shown for each contrast.
main.4: Risk-ranked review curves and external paired contrasts. Panels A and B show empirical step curves of the fraction of low-quality patients detected versus the actual number selected for simulated review, ranked by descending risk with official CaseID as the lexicographic tie-breaker. The cohorts contain 93/851 and 16/252 low-quality patients, respectively (Dice <0.70). Blue solid and orange dashed curves represent Methods A and B. Filled squares mark the development-locked cutoffs (internal A: 71/93 detected at 174 reviews; B: 68/93 at 150; external A: 10/16 at 35; B: 13/16 at 33). Open circles mark 50 external reviews per method (A: 14/16; B: 13/16). Panel C shows B minus A detection differences with the original paired nominal 95 % Newcombe method 10 intervals: +18.75 [−4.28, +40.04] percentage points at locked cutoffs and −6.25 [−31.61, +19.57] at top 50. The latter interval conditions on the observed ranking and does not account for re-ranking in another sample.
main.5: Three shared screening misses in the external set. Rows show case089 (A–C), case175 (D–F), and case238 (G–I); columns show the original released RGB ultrasound image, the released reference contour (blue), and the actual initial CPU replay prediction contour (orange). Row values are CPU replay Dice against the reference and risks A and B, rather than the original archived CUDA scores. All panels preserve the full original image field and aspect ratio. In case175, the nonempty prediction includes a thin upper-edge band. Masks were captured in the six-case exact-checkpoint CPU replay; no new model inference was performed to create this figure. Original CUDA scores and primary study estimates were retained unchanged.

supplement.S1: Sensitivity to the Dice definition of low quality with development-locked risk cutoffs unchanged. Panel A shows Method A detection in the BrEaST external test minus BUS-BRA internal holdout. Panel B shows paired Method B minus Method A detection in BrEaST. Low-quality denominators for Dice <0.50, <0.70, and <0.80 are 53, 93, and 183 internally and 7, 16, and 50 externally. Points show the original differences in percentage points and bars the original nominal two-sided 95 % Newcombe method 10 confidence intervals. No interval was replaced by a bootstrap interval.
supplement.S2: Paired detection outcomes for the same 16 BrEaST external low-quality patients (Dice <0.70), under two review policies. Panel A uses development-locked cutoffs: both methods detect 10 patients, Method A only 0, Method B only 3, and neither 3; the corresponding review counts are 35/252 for A and 33/252 for B. Panel B uses the top 50 ranked patients per method: both detect 12, A only 2, B only 1, and neither 1. The four mutually exclusive outcome categories sum to 16 under each policy. The locked-cutoff A-only cell has zero observed support.
supplement.S3: Review-budget transfer and detection across all eight evaluated budgets (5 %, 10 %, 15 %, 20 %, 25 %, 30 %, 40 %, and 50 %). (A) Observed review fractions after transferring development-calibrated thresholds to the internal holdout (filled markers, solid lines; n=851) and external cohort (open markers, dashed lines; n=252); the dotted diagonal marks equality with the target budget. (B,C) Observed low-quality detection on the external (16 low-quality cases) and internal (93 low-quality cases) cohorts. Filled markers/solid lines denote transferred thresholds, and open markers/dashed lines denote cohort-specific equal-review ranking. Method A uses blue circles and method B uses orange diamonds in A–C; shapes retain method identity in grayscale. (D) External paired B-minus-A detection differences (percentage points); points are observed contrasts, and vertical bars are the archived paired Newcombe 95 % confidence intervals. Dark circles denote transferred thresholds and blue open squares denote equal review; horizontal offsets are for legibility only. The equal-review count is cohort-specific and rounded as archived; at the 20 % budget, 50 of 252 external cases are reviewed per method. Lines in A–C connect observed budget settings and do not imply additional evaluations.
supplement.S4: Exploratory bootstrap stability under three sources of variation. R1 resamples test patients at fixed development cutoffs; R2 resamples development patients for cutoff calibration while holding the test cohorts fixed; R3 resamples development and test patients. Each route has 10,000 archived patient-bootstrap replicates with method A, method B, and quality labels kept paired. (A) Method-A external-minus-internal contrasts for H1, low-quality detection (filled circles), and H2, review fraction (open squares). (B) External B-minus-A detection contrasts for the fixed-cutoff policy (dark circles) and equal top-50 review policy (blue open squares). In A and B, points are bootstrap medians and horizontal bars are unadjusted 2.5th–97.5th percentile intervals from the archived valid replicates; a collapsed interval is shown by its point, including the necessarily constant R2 equal-top-50 endpoint. (C) Exact empirical frequencies among jointly valid replicates, with marker shapes identifying four mutually exclusive sign categories. Original strict means fixed B−A >0 and top-50 B−A <0; opposite strict reverses both inequalities; any zero includes either contrast equal to zero; same nonzero means both contrasts share a nonzero sign. Frequencies are not p-values, posterior probabilities, or population probabilities. The observed external fixed-cutoff A-only detection cell is zero: R1 cannot resample an A-only detection and its fixed B−A distribution is therefore structurally nonnegative. Its [0,40] pp percentile interval does not exclude a population A advantage and does not replace the original paired Newcombe interval [−4.28,40.04] pp. Only 16 external low-quality patients inform detection; bootstrap replicates are not new patients.
supplement.S5: Descriptive symmetric Kitagawa decomposition of external-minus-internal differences at the locked development-calibrated cutoffs. (A) Low-quality detection. (B) Review fraction. For each outcome, the total observed difference is separated into a diagnostic-composition-associated term and a within-stratum-rate term using dataset-reported benign and malignant strata. Blue filled circles denote method A, and orange open squares denote method B; points are observed estimates, and horizontal bars are each term's own unadjusted bootstrap percentile 95 % interval. The symmetric formula averages internal and external stratum rates for the composition term and averages internal and external stratum weights for the within-stratum term. Detection weights use low-quality denominators; review weights use all-patient denominators. The two panels use separately labeled horizontal scales. There were 5,000 archived patient-bootstrap draws; detection components have 4,999 valid draws because one draw had an undefined external benign low-quality rate, while detection totals and all review terms have 5,000 valid draws. Observed terms add to their total; percentile-interval endpoints do not have to add. This is post hoc descriptive accounting, not causal attribution or a percent-explained analysis; two diagnostic strata do not remove other confounding. Only 16 external low-quality cases inform detection, and bootstrap draws are not independent new patients.
supplement.S6: Actual prompt-shift responses in the six-case CPU replay. S6A contains shared misses case089 (A), case175 (B), and case238 (C); S6B contains B-only detections case024 (D), case105 (E), and case222 (F). Each case panel shows the reference (blue) and initial CPU prediction (orange) at left. The right 2 × 2 grid shows actual predictions after left (top left), right (top right), up (bottom left), and down (bottom right) prompt shifts; orange denotes the displayed CPU prediction, blue the same reference, and dashed gray the actual prompt box. Each D value is the Dice between that shifted prediction and the initial CPU prediction, rather than its Dice against the reference. Row values give initial CPU Dice against the reference and risks A/B. All 30 nonempty prediction masks from the six existing patients are shown, with original RGB pixels, full fields of view, and unchanged mask geometry. The case175 masks touch the upper image boundary; the right-shift prediction is a narrow nonempty band. CPU masks are not the unarchived original CUDA masks, and original CUDA scores were not overwritten. These six cases are not additional independent patients.
